speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you're experiencing shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if the pain is sharp, burning, or throbbing?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Occipital Neuralgia (or greater auricular nerve entrapment/irritation) secondary to tympanoplasty scar tissue or surgical manipulation. The "shooting" quality of pain and difficulty with earrings suggest nerve involvement rather than simple infection, especially given the 12-week post-op timeline. REQUEST IMAGES: Post-op CT Temporal Bone and MRI of the Temporal Bone with contrast.
